name: Thomas Petersen
event: UFC Fight Night: Bonfim vs. Brady
summary: A 32-year-old heavyweight wrestler (11-5; 3-4 UFC; Spartan MMA) taking this fight on about two weeks' notice, three-and-a-half months after Valter Walker submitted him with a calf slicer in 92 seconds. He alternates wins and losses in the UFC: he beats the lower tier with wrestling and clinch control and gets stopped by stronger strikers.

how_they_fight.Striking: Utility striking to close distance; better on the regional scene (seven KO/TKOs, six in R1). Against Pat he dropped him twice in R3 (short right hook, uppercut) after two slow rounds (Cageside). Accurate (about 55%) but low-volume.
how_they_fight.Grappling: His main weapon: clinches against the fence, single legs, body locks, knees to the thighs. Went 9 for 9 with nearly 14 minutes of control against Don'Tale Mayes; 0 for 5 against Pat but still had 8:36 of control. Walker caught him in leg locks on the mat (heel hook, then calf slicer).
how_they_fight.Defense: The problem: four of his five losses were stoppages. Waldo Cortes-Acosta TKO R3 (4:53, LFA 2022), Shamil Gaziev TKO R1 (2025), Vitor Petrino KO R3 (0:26, after being dropped in R1, 2025), Walker sub R1 (2026). He ducks his head into uppercuts (Cageside, on Petrino).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: UFC wins are all decisions, built on control. Losses come either early to power (Gaziev R1, Walker R1) or late after he's been worn down or dropped (Cortes-Acosta and Petrino in R3). Against Pat he got stronger in R3. He's a lighter heavyweight (245 for Walker).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Knows his lane: clinch, wrestle, grind. LowKick's view after Walker: good enough to beat the bottom of the division, outmatched against ranked opposition.

patterns: Clinch and wrestling control; UFC wins all by decision
Stopped by heavier hitters (Gaziev, Petrino, Cortes-Acosta)
Two of four stoppage losses in R3, two in R1
Can raise his output late (Pat, R3)
concerns: Short notice, about 15 weeks after a submission loss
Chin and defense against power punchers
Our data has the Pat fight as a split decision; Cageside and LowKick report a majority decision (28-28, 29-27, 29-27)
keys_to_beat: Stop the first takedowns and hit him on the way in
Uppercuts as he ducks into the clinch

news.text: Stepped in on short notice to face Gabriel Lourenco after Alvin Hines withdrew.
Submitted by Valter Walker with a calf slicer in 92 seconds (first calf slicer win by a UFC heavyweight, per LowKick).
Beat Guilherme Pat by majority decision (per Cageside; our data says split) after two R3 knockdowns.
